# T001: Session store, types and expiry fixtures

## Goal
When this task is done, `src/auth/store.ts` implements the `SessionStore` contract with an in-memory map, `src/auth/types.ts` exports the `Session`, `SessionStore` and `TokenCodec` types exactly as written in the spec, and the expiry arithmetic is pinned by a fixture table the owner has reviewed. The refresh cases in the table are present but skipped; T003 un-skips them.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a store and `now = 0`, When `create("u1", 0)` is called with `sessionMinutes: 30`, Then the session has a 32-character hex id and `expiresAt` of 1,800,000.
- Given a session that expires at 1,800,000, When `get(id, 1_800_000)` is called, Then it returns `null` and a second `get` at any time also returns `null`.
- Given a session that expires at 1,800,000, When `get(id, 1_799_999)` is called, Then the session is returned unchanged.
- Given the fixture table `test/fixtures/sessions.json`, When the unit tests run, Then every `get` case passes and every `touch` case is reported as skipped, not failed.

## Target files
- src/auth/store.ts
- src/auth/types.ts
- test/auth/store.test.ts
- test/fixtures/sessions.json

## Contracts
- SessionStore (spec.md §Contracts)

## Out of scope
- Refresh logic in `touch` (T003). Implement `touch` as a stub that returns `get(id, now)`.
- Any HTTP route (T002, T004).

## Notes for the worker
Start with the fixture table: one array of `{ name, session, now, expected }` for `get` and one for `touch`, with the `touch` array marked `"pending": "T003"`. Then write the store against the `get` cases. Keep the store free of clock reads; the caller passes `now`. The owner reviews the fixture table before merge, so leave a short comment at the top of the JSON saying what each column means.
